reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that higher sintering temperature and longer time increase density and thermal conductivity by forming a more complete copper 3D network, but it does not mention SPS, rapid heating, high pressure, controlled cooling, or any comparison with conventional sintering. It provides no support for the specific SPS mechanism, the 10% enhancement claim, or the preservation of mechanical and irradiation properties.
premises: SPS on chemically plated W–20Cu produces a highly densified microstructure with an interconnected copper network
An interconnected copper network enhances thermal conductivity by minimizing phonon scattering
SPS prevents tungsten grain coarsening while accelerating copper rearrangement
A ~10% enhancement in thermal conductivity is achievable relative to conventionally sintered samples
Mechanical durability and irradiation resistance are preserved at levels comparable to conventional processing
